newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Metals - Zinc premium surges on volatility.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Metals - Zinc premium surges on volatility.

text.p: Taipei base metal traders said on Tuesday that spot zinc premiums had surged to US$120-150 a tonne in Taiwan from $85-95 a tonne a week ago as suppliers sought refuge from volatility in the world zinc market.
"Zinc suppliers are asking for more premiums to cover their risks," said a buyer at Taiwan steelmaker Kao Hsing Chang.
Traders said some suppliers also were using the high premiums to curb buying interest.
"Some suppliers would rather take to the sidelines," another buyer said.
Traders said local suppliers were uncertain about London Metal Exchange zinc prices, carefully watching factors like China smelters' major short positions and possible corrections.
"China's large short zinc positions will support the futures prices, but a correction is always possible," a trader said.
China producers have been short for up to 250,000 tonnes of zinc on the LME at around $1,100 a tonne since late 1996, traders said.
Chinese producers faced major losses as LME zinc prices had marched to a seven-year high of $1,675 a tonne on Monday and three-month delivery had settled to $1,671 at the close.
One estimate puts the losses of Chinese zinc producers at up to US$100 million.
Traders said Taiwan aluminium and copper import premiums remained unchanged due to slow local market.
